honesty.banner: Sample / demo dataset — not a live intelligence feed. These briefs are illustrative and labeled. They are not current-event reports.
honesty.confidenceRules: Observed is reserved for established facts. Predicted downstream effects must never use Observed. Missing or invalid confidence defaults to Unknown.

articles.headline: Canal authority reduces daily transit slots after prolonged drought
articles.factualSummary: In this sample scenario, a canal operator publishes a status notice reducing daily vessel transit slots after months of below-normal rainfall. The notice cites lower water levels and asks carriers to expect longer waits.

waypointsTake.whyItMatters: A chokepoint many import schedules assume will stay open can tighten without a single dramatic accident — drought-driven slot cuts are structural capacity loss.
waypointsTake.analysis: Carriers and ports on either approach face queues and missed connections within days to weeks. Some cargo may reroute via longer lanes before consumer shelves thin. Recovery depends on rainfall and water management — those timelines are not knowable from the notice alone.

likelyImpactPath.label: Canal slot cuts
likelyImpactPath.explanation: Operator notice reduces daily transit capacity.

likelyImpactPath.label: Canal corridor
likelyImpactPath.explanation: Shared chokepoint queues vessels on either approach.

likelyImpactPath.explanation: Schedules slip; some cargo seeks longer alternate lanes.

likelyImpactPath.explanation: Inventory timing and intermediate parts face delay risk.

likelyImpactPath.label: Goods availability
likelyImpactPath.explanation: Households may notice slower restocks — not an overnight shock.

articles.headline: Government announces higher tariffs on selected steel imports
articles.factualSummary: In this sample scenario, a trade authority publishes a notice raising tariff rates on selected steel product lines. The notice lists covered product codes and an effective date.

waypointsTake.whyItMatters: Tariffs change the relative cost of imported inputs before most households see anything — the first relationship that matters is steel to manufacturing to construction.
waypointsTake.analysis: Importers and fabricators face higher landed costs once the effective date arrives. Downstream effects on housing materials are plausible over months but not automatic. Pass-through depends on contracts, inventories, and domestic capacity.

likelyImpactPath.label: Steel tariff
likelyImpactPath.explanation: Published tariff schedule takes effect on listed lines.

likelyImpactPath.label: Steel
likelyImpactPath.explanation: Landed cost of covered imports rises for importers.

likelyImpactPath.label: Manufacturing
likelyImpactPath.explanation: Fabricators face input-cost pressure.

likelyImpactPath.label: Construction
likelyImpactPath.explanation: Project budgets may absorb higher material costs.

likelyImpactPath.label: Housing costs
likelyImpactPath.explanation: Pass-through to housing materials is plausible, not certain.

articles.headline: Carriers divert sailings away from a contested maritime corridor
articles.factualSummary: In this sample scenario, a maritime advisory notes that several carriers are diverting sailings away from a contested corridor after security incidents. Public notices describe longer alternate routes and schedule uncertainty.

waypointsTake.whyItMatters: Security risk at a strait can move freight onto longer routes quickly — the first-order link is corridor risk to voyage days to fuel and schedule cost.
waypointsTake.analysis: Longer transit times and higher bunker fuel use appear within days for diverted voyages. Port congestion elsewhere and delayed intermediate goods are plausible over weeks. How long diversions continue is contingent on security conditions.

likelyImpactPath.label: Corridor diversion
likelyImpactPath.explanation: Carriers divert sailings after security advisories.

likelyImpactPath.label: Longer sea route
likelyImpactPath.explanation: Voyages add days via alternate Capes.

likelyImpactPath.label: Freight / fuel
likelyImpactPath.explanation: Bunker burn and schedule cost rise.

likelyImpactPath.label: Logistics / retail
likelyImpactPath.explanation: Inventory buffers and port congestion adjust.

likelyImpactPath.label: Goods & fuel costs
likelyImpactPath.explanation: Later arrivals and possible fuel sensitivity — analysis only.

articles.headline: Ransomware disrupts a major fuel pipeline operator’s billing systems
articles.factualSummary: In this sample scenario based on a well-known historical pattern, a pipeline operator reports a ransomware incident affecting business systems and temporarily pauses some operations. Public advisories describe precautionary shutdowns.

waypointsTake.whyItMatters: Cyber incidents on energy operators can halt physical flows even when malware hits IT systems — the relationship is cyber event to critical infrastructure to fuel distribution.
waypointsTake.analysis: Spot shortages and panic-buying risk can appear within days in dependent regions if product stops moving. Restoration timelines often remain partly opaque during the incident. Predicted household price paths must not be labeled as Observed.

likelyImpactPath.label: Ransomware
likelyImpactPath.explanation: Operator reports ransomware affecting business systems.

likelyImpactPath.explanation: Precautionary pause can halt product movement.
